Scones punish a warm hand. The butter has to stay in cold flakes until the oven melts it, or the rise never comes.

Grate the butter straight from the freezer. Toss it through the flour with a fork, never your fingers. The bowl should smell of nothing but flour and a little salt.

Add the buttermilk in one pour and stop the moment the dough holds. Three folds, no more. Overworked dough bakes flat and tight, like a biscuit that lost its nerve.

Cut straight down with a floured cutter. A twist seals the edge and the scone leans as it rises. Brush only the tops with egg, so the sides stay free to climb.

Bake them close together at 220 degrees for twelve minutes. They prop each other up. When the kitchen smells of hot butter and toasted milk, they are nearly there.

Before the oven door shuts, check the shelf is in the top third. Lower down, the bottoms scorch before the tops colour.
